text: A survey of 12,000 young office workers saw blood pressure fall 11 points, but only among those who cut salt.
Coffee gave sleep-deprived university students a 2 percent memory boost, on a single word-list test.
Working from home boosted productivity in three startups' software teams, but the reported gains vanished after six months.
The new bridge saved bus passengers about twenty minutes on average, compared with a year of roadworks.
Vitamin D may prevent colds, but that was seen only in under-fives in one supplement-funded winter trial.
A reading app helped children learning English as a second language, but the gains faded by the next school year.
A pesticide study in two English counties found bumblebee colonies produced a quarter fewer queens in one season.
A four-day week in Icelandic public offices reduced burnout, with pay unchanged and no change in sick days.
